reason: Rich's stated design is a memory knowledge graph: memories extend and reference each other, nodes are not spokes. Agents instead attach every memory straight to its node with no relations, so the map shows a dandelion. The rule for recording memories is a class of work of its own, not covered by the metaform-development memory notes.

Rich's 2026-10-15 model supersedes the node-joined rule in this skill. Memories and knowledge attach through knowledge layers linked at a base map address; the link moves down by itself to the common prefix; memories linked from a layer are transitive. The old body says a node is where memories are joined and gives agents no placement rule, which is what produced the one-node-per-memory dandelion. The description needs the placement and layer triggers so the skill loads when a knowledge layer is being placed.

Episode aligned the link-placement rule (base link moves down, never up), transitive memories, and the paper as governing design text; the skill still told agents to place at the most general address in some copies and did not point to the paper.

The trigger is too narrow: the design talk about where knowledge applies and how it is pushed to agents never loaded this skill, and the assistant proposed a spec round the paper already answered. Broaden the trigger so design discussion of memory placement and push loads it.

Resend-after-compaction is no longer just design: it depends on ACP reporting compaction, which needs the client to advertise session.compaction. Point the rule at the new skill so the held design is not built on a false assumption.

Rich corrected the framing: medium is only one example and every property layer is the same kind. The skill named medium as the special case; a port of any property is a layer swap, and genre (platformer.3d) binds at a function like any other property.

The push trigger was restated in this episode: compaction does not trigger a push, it only clears the sent record, and the next push comes with work at a node. The old line made compaction the resend trigger, which would push too early and keep firing wrongly.

Rich stated two rules that the skill lacks: never gate or judge the model's inference (enforce mechanics only), and the per-node note is a show-once push, not a memory. Both govern how memory and knowledge reach agents.

The existing line says the link moves "down" to the common prefix and "never up". That contradicts line 21 (never toward the leaves) and Rich's rule: the common prefix is nearer the trunk, so the link moves up. Also adds the worked example Rich asked for.

Rich required that tickets be explicit about relinking toward the trunk. The episode shows the rule was pushed onto tickets by hand after the fact; the skill should say tickets carry it from the start.

The person's note now reaches agents through the dispatch hand-off (VIEW-034 amendment, ticket code.graph.knowledge#d), and the base-holds-no-note rule was added to MAP-046 and built into writes.base_only. This skill governs knowledge placement and still described the note only as pushed-once-per-session design, so it should name the current delivery and the base rule.
Recording a memory at a deleted element failed; the working recovery (re-attach to the RE that took over the goal) is not written anywhere.

The spec drafts called code.python and code.rust "layers", and the user twice had to correct that there is no layer called code. The rule text itself invited the mistake by calling every property a layer.

The root-name guard now lands in layering.create and layering.rename. The skill states the rule but not its exact reach, so an agent could over-read it and refuse valid `<scope>@<content>` layer names.
